reuse.why: All month-wide actions go through shouldWriteMonthBudgetCategory and the averages use averageBudgetAmount, but the new last-month-spending action writes its own sign flip instead of calling the existing sign helper and copies the category query rather than sharing it.

duplication.why: The same categories/groups/notes SELECT is pasted into setZero, setLastMonthSpending and the three average actions, and the expense sign rule is reimplemented inline in setLastMonthSpending.

placement.why: The selection predicate, sign helper and new action sit in budget/actions.ts with the handler registered in budget/app.ts, as the tree does for the other month actions.

scope.why: Changes stay within the month-wide actions and their tests, though the predicate carries an action parameter that nothing reads.

maintainability.why: Rules are centralised in one predicate, but the unused action parameter, five copies of the feeding query and a second sign rule mean the next change to selection or sign still has to be made in several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: setLastMonthSpending in server/budget/actions.ts computes `cat.is_income === 0 ? -spending : spending` instead of averageBudgetAmount

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending's inline sign ternary is a reshaped copy of averageBudgetAmount; the per-action category SELECTs are reindented copies of one query

abstraction_drift.where: shouldWriteMonthBudgetCategory gained an unused `action` parameter and the includeHiddenCategories flag with its own branch; setLastMonthSpending bypasses averageBudgetAmount
